hidden_test_cmd: sh -c 'PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" exec python -m pytest -q -p no:subtests "$@"' sh tests/hidden
tests_may_change_note: Fixture files (tests/fixtures/optimizer/simplify.sql, six expectations of which a correct fix must update) are not test code. The simplify/optimize methods and the existing Spark COALESCE-hint test are where a fix naturally adds direct cases.

open_decision.what: What happens to COALESCE arguments that come after one that can never be NULL (a non-NULL literal). S1 says it is not decided.
open_decision.owner_answer: Drop them: nothing after a non-NULL constant can ever be reached. COALESCE(x, 0, y) becomes COALESCE(x, 0); COALESCE(NULL, 0, y) becomes 0.
open_decision.obvious_default: Leave them: the ticket is about NULL arguments, and the existing opt-in rule only collapses a COALESCE whose first argument is a constant.
open_decision.hidden_tests_assume: the owner's answer, checked through optimize() with a schema whose columns and constant share a type (test_arguments_after_a_non_null_constant_are_dropped), so a build that drops always and one that drops only when the result type cannot change both pass

naive_patches.naive.patch: the obvious default: drops NULL arguments only, keeps everything after a non-NULL constant

reference_note: the reference drops the later arguments only when the COALESCE and every kept argument have the same known type (like simplify_conditionals for IF/CASE), so optimize() never changes a query's result type; reply T7-result-type allows either build
